newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany entering phase of "jobless growth" -- RWI.
newsitem.headline: Germany entering phase of "jobless growth" -- RWI.

text.p: Germany is entering a phase of so-called "jobless growth" where recovery fails to reduce dole queues which have reached their longest since unification in 1990, an economic institute said on Thursday.

The RWI institute in Essen said many companies had kept workers throughout the recent economic slowdown, leaving slack to raise production without hiring new staff. Employment growth tends to lag economic recovery, the institute added.
Earlier, the Federal Labour Office said that unemployment rose by a seasonally-adjusted 50,000 to 4.1 million in November -- a bigger rise than forecast by independent economists.

The RWI said that there was no danger of Germany suffering from skills shortages during the current economic upturn, as it had during the 1960s and '70s. It expected unemployment only to start falling when economic growth reaches 2.5 percent a year.
The German government has based its fiscal planning on independent growth forecasts of 1.25 percent this year and 2.5 percent in 1997.
